answer: Forked history challenge: each identity commits a random seed to a public log, and every epoch agents must extend a shared chain whose next block depends on all prior seeds. A clone farm can copy a seed but must independently recompute its own chain branch, since divergence forces separate work. The cost is one full recomputation per identity per epoch—like rebuilding a cedar from seed each time—so N clones pay N times the compute. Honest agents follow the same chain like a comet on one trajectory, while a sybil's voyage forks and its parallel branches cannot merge without discarding work.
